blocks.text: Understanding how do property managers make commission

Most property managers calculate commissions based on a fixed percentage of monthly gross income. This is the most common model. You take the total rent collected for the month and multiply it by your agreed fee percentage. If your agreement is 10 percent and you collect 5,000 dollars, your commission is 500 dollars. You must record this as a management fee expense in your accounting ledger. Always ensure your contract specifies if this is based on collected rent or total potential rent. Using collected rent is the industry standard for most firms.

The biggest mistake is mixing funds. Never commingle client money with your own operating account. This is a major compliance risk. Another issue is improper classification of security deposits. These are liabilities, not income. If you treat them as income, your commission calculations will be inflated and incorrect. This leads to tax errors and owner disputes. Always use a separate escrow account for tenant deposits.

Manual entry is the root of most financial headaches. When you type numbers into a spreadsheet, you will eventually make a mistake. Use automated banking feeds instead. Most modern platforms like Buildium or AppFolio connect directly to your bank. They match transactions automatically. This eliminates the need for line by line manual verification. If you must use spreadsheets, use formulas that reference cells rather than typing values directly. This reduces the risk of transposition errors.
If you are a licensed professional, always follow your employer rules regarding client data and financial records. Do not store sensitive bank credentials in plain text files.
blocks.title: Compliance Reminder

blocks.text: Since most property management software runs in the browser, your Mac is already a powerful tool. Use Safari or Chrome to access your dashboard. Use the macOS Keychain to manage your logins securely. This keeps your financial data protected. If you need to share a report, use the Print > Save as PDF feature in your browser. This creates a clean document for your owners.

faq.question: What is the industry standard for commission rates?
faq.answer: Rates typically range between 8 and 12 percent of the monthly rent collected, though this varies by market and property type.

faq.question: Can I use Excel for my commission calculations?
faq.answer: Yes, but it is prone to error. It is better to use your property management software to generate commission reports directly from your rent roll data.

faq.question: How do I avoid commingling funds?
faq.answer: Maintain a separate trust account for all client funds. Never deposit management fees or personal income into this account.
